newsitem.title: USA: Texaco gains on Q1, retreats on crude price.
newsitem.headline: Texaco gains on Q1, retreats on crude price.

text.p: Texaco Inc's share price was boosted by strong first quarter results but later retreated due to weakness in the crude oil price, analysts said.
By 1210 EST/1610 GMT the stock was up 7/8 at 105-1/4 after having been as high as 106. Texaco's first quarter earnings came in above consensus forecasts.
"People had expected a big day on the crude markets, but it is off over $0.50 a barrel," said Frank Knuettel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
May West Texas Intermediate blend was quoted down $0.56 at $19.82.
Texaco reported first quarter operating income of $1.84 per share, compared with analysts' consensus estimate of $1.72. A year earlier the company earned $1.42 a share.

Texaco's exploration and production operating earnings were strong, rising to $467 million from $397 million a year earlier, but international refining and marketing took a hit in Asia, where refined product sales at Texaco's part-owned Caltex unit fell to 586,000 barrels per day from 712,000.
Overall international product sales declined to 1.46 millon barrels a day from 1.65 million a year ago, and U.S. product sales slipped slightly to 1.0 million barrels per day.
"There is too much Asian capacity; 1.4 million barrels of capacity has been built, so it is not surprising that Caltex should have a hard time," said Knuettel.
